blocks.explanation:
Substitute \(t = \sqrt{x}\) (\(dx = 2t\,dt\)) to get \(2\int t^2\sin t\,dt\).
Plan: integrate by parts twice with the power of \(t\) as the first function.
steps:
Given: \(\int \sqrt{x}\sin\sqrt{x}\,dx\), \(x > 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: substitute \(t = \sqrt{x}\), \(dx = 2t\,dt\); then integrate \(2\int t^2\sin t\,dt\) by parts twice.

Substitute
\[x = t^2,\ dx = 2t\,dt\]
\[\int t\sin t\cdot 2t\,dt = 2\int t^2\sin t\,dt\]
Why: \(\sqrt{x} = t\) and \(dx = 2t\,dt\).

First integration by parts
\[\int t^2\sin t\,dt = -t^2\cos t + \int 2t\cos t\,dt\]
Why: \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\), \(\frac{d}{dt}t^2 = 2t\).

Second integration by parts
\[\int 2t\cos t\,dt = 2t\sin t - \int 2\sin t\,dt\]
\[= 2t\sin t + 2\cos t\]
Why: \(2t\) first, \(\cos t\) second; \(\int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t\).

Combine and multiply by 2
\[2\int t^2\sin t\,dt = -2t^2\cos t + 4t\sin t + 4\cos t + c\]
\[= -2x\cos\sqrt{x} + 4\sqrt{x}\sin\sqrt{x} + 4\cos\sqrt{x} + c\]
Why: \(t = \sqrt{x}\), \(t^2 = x\).

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dt}(-2t^2\cos t + 4t\sin t + 4\cos t)\]
\[= -4t\cos t + 2t^2\sin t + 4\sin t + 4t\cos t - 4\sin t\]
\[= 2t^2\sin t\]
Why: and \(2t^2\sin t\,dt = \sqrt{x}\sin\sqrt{x}\cdot 2t\,dt = \sqrt{x}\sin\sqrt{x}\,dx\).
